newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper ends higher for third session.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper ends higher for third session.

text.p: COMEX copper rallied for the third straight session Wednesday, in line with LME copper which gained strength from a sharp fall in LME warehouse stocks.

"Copper looks to have a short term upward bias, with an upcoming 10,000-12,000 tonne draw in LME copper stocks being talked about for Friday's data, after the 8,000 tonne draw Tuesday, and the stocks seen moving to Asia,," Merrill Lynch senior commodities strategist, Bill O'Neill said.
COMEX December copper ended up 0.55 cent at 89.70 cents, continuing the recovering from three month lows at 84.50 cents seen on September 12.
LME copper warehouse stocks fell 8,825 tonnes Tuesday to 256,625 tonnes, but COMEX copper stocks rose 642 short tons to 21,274 short tons Tuesday.
But the contract may find resistance again near 91 cents, where the rally failed last week, analysts said.
December copper has traded between 84.50 and 90.95 cents in the past three weeks, and continues to lack much direction, traders said.

The December/March backwardation ended little changed at 0.80 cent, from 0.70 cent at Tuesday's close, after narrowing from 2.30 cent on August 30, while the COMEX December/LME three month arbitrage remained little changed at a 2.11 cent premium in favor of COMEX.
